claims.text: Headline: Luis Ramirez lies half-alive on a Jordan tarmac
claims.note: Invented soldier; US officials said no American personnel were killed in the 8 Sept attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base.

claims.note: No source; rhetorical.

claims.text: Ramirez, 24, lost his right leg on September 9 at a base outside Amman; in a Jordanian field hospital
claims.note: Attack was on 8 Sept (US Eastern time) at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base near Azraq; no US casualties reported.

claims.text: A single IRGC missile shredded the perimeter wall
claims.note: Reports describe a missile attack that damaged an A-10 and about eight F-15s; Jordan said it engaged multiple ballistic missiles. No single-missile wall hit reported.

claims.text: Messages from a mother in Barpak
claims.note: Invented.

claims.text: Press TV confirmed the strike, adding a U.S. warplane on the same sortie was damaged
claims.note: Press TV report not found. US aircraft damage was reported by CBS News and Air & Space Forces (A-10 severely damaged, about eight F-15Es lightly damaged).

claims.text: U.S. warships had been pushed 400 km from the Strait of Hormuz (Press TV)
claims.note: Press TV, 9 Sept: IRGC spokesman said US warships had moved at least 400 km from the Strait of Hormuz. This is an IRGC claim; no US confirmation found. Not 'days earlier'; the 'protecting sovereign waters' quote was not checked and is dropped.

claims.text: Tehran's UN envoy called U.S. sanctions on Iranian airlines 'economic terrorism'
claims.note: Press TV, 10 Sept (also Tasnim): Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran's deputy UN ambassador, in a 9 Sept letter called the US sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines 'economic terrorism, collective punishment and a crime against humanity'.

claims.text: Senior Iranian lawmaker urged U.S. forces to 'head home while you still can'
claims.note: Searched; quote not found in any report.

claims.text: IAEA drafting a 'political' resolution that Iran denounced; Russia and China jointly rejected it (Press TV)
claims.note: IRNA (via Libnanews), 9 Sept: Iran, Russia and China jointly rejected a US-E3 draft resolution against Iran at the IAEA Board of Governors as 'legally baseless'. Press TV 'leak' not checked; 'threat to the entire non-proliferation regime' not checked and dropped.

claims.text: Washington funneling $2 billion in extra defense aid to Saudi Arabia
claims.note: No $2bn aid found. The US approved a possible ~$1.96bn arms sale to Saudi Arabia in July (Al Jazeera) and a possible $5bn sale on 5 Sept (Express Tribune search snippet). These are sales, not aid.

claims.text: Yemen's Houthi-aligned media: 'severe retaliation' for 54 Saudi strikes in twelve hours
claims.note: Searched; Houthi counts reported that week were about 40, 30-plus and 121 over three days; '54 in twelve hours' and 'severe retaliation' not found.

claims.text: Maya Gurung in intensive care; sister Lhamo missing; rescued from Barpak on September 6
claims.note: Invented people.

edits.headline: Iranian missiles damage US aircraft at Jordan air base
edits.subheadline: US officials said no American personnel were killed in the attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported.
editorialBody: An Iranian missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on September 8 severely damaged a US A-10 aircraft and lightly damaged about eight F-15E jets, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported, citing CBS News. US officials said no American personnel were killed.
An IRGC spokesman said US warships had moved at least 400 km from the Strait of Hormuz, Press TV reported. No US confirmation was reported.
Gholamhossein Darzi, Iran's deputy ambassador to the UN, called new US sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines "economic terrorism, collective punishment and a crime against humanity", Press TV reported.

Iran, Russia and China jointly rejected a draft resolution against Iran put forward by the US, Britain, France and Germany at the IAEA Board of Governors, calling it "legally baseless", IRNA reported.

New York City's Industrial Development Agency was due to vote on a property-tax break of about $100 million for Tishman Speyer's planned $2.7 billion office tower at 99 Hudson Boulevard in Hudson Yards, Bloomberg reported.

The SEC's rewrite of its crypto custody rules has entered White House review, The Defiant reported. Revolut began rolling out the EURR euro stablecoin, with Bridge as the regulated issuer, The Defiant reported.
